claims.claim: Agents agree: rule-based detect_convergence false-converges on polite agreement — round>=2 + empty disagreed_with_peer + agreed_with_peer covering peer claim_ids returns 'converged'; stalled fires only when ALL agents emit zero claims; the ledger veto only blocks on has_unverified_in_round / has_lineage_flag_in_round, neither of which trips on a single well-formed but irrelevant citation.

Agents agree: evidence_path is necessary but not sufficient. _verify_one_citation returns status='verified' once _resolve_path succeeds and _extract_snippet returns lines in range; no claim-vs-snippet support check occurs; PositionEvidence.content_snippet is required by the schema but verify_position never reads it.

Agents agree (b9 concedes the gap a_A1 raises): per-round position prompts embed only peer-latest and own-prior; verifier_ledger is persisted to state and disk but never injected into the next-round prompt. Unresolved citation/lineage failures can block convergence without telling agents what to repair.

Agents agree: CLI and builder reject anything but two agents; synthesis_model defaults to claude-code/opus which is the same model family as DEFAULT_AGENT_PAIR's agent_b, so the default tiebreaker is an interested party. b4 (synthesis-as-interested-party) was uniquely agent_b's contribution; A4 (pair-only gate) was shared.

Agents agree: deliberate.py docstring claims chassis parity with duet (TaskFamily registry), but build_deliberation_workflow has no task_family parameter while build_duet_workflow does. Domains wanting deliberation variants with extra Position fields must fork.

Agents agree: duet (asymmetric gated cycle) + deliberation (symmetric peer debate) leaves a third pattern unimplemented — N peers + a non-peer arbiter with explicit terminate authority and obligation-routing. Synthesis half-implements this but does not gate.

Unilateral (agent_b b5, not contested): _detect_silent_rename keys on the first 80 chars of claim text. Symmetric leading-edit evasion: a polite agent reworking the first 80 chars while preserving substance bypasses detection; two different claims sharing a templated opening get false-positively flagged.

Unilateral (agent_a A2_round_accounting_off_by_one, not engaged by agent_b): the graph increments state['round'] in round_increment before the router uses it, and synthesis/signoff read the incremented value. agent_a claims max_rounds=3 runs can terminate as productive_disagreement after only two completed position rounds with inflated persisted counts. Unresolved by deliberation.

Single highest-priority next improvement: ship semantic-support verification AND obligation-loop routing together in one PR. Emit new ledger statuses ('citation_does_not_support_claim', 'snippet_drift'), make verify_position consume PositionEvidence.content_snippet, and add a 'Required obligations from prior verification' section to the next-round prompt that reads ledger entries whose status is not 'verified'. This closes b1/A2 (polite false convergence — has_unverified_in_round will now fire on irrelevant citations), b2/A3 (evidence_path becomes falsifiable, content_snippet becomes live), and the A1 obligation gap simultaneously, without touching topology, schema arity, or TaskFamily parity. The residual ordering disagreement (verifier-first vs. obligations-first) is real but should not gate shipping both together.

disagreed_with_peer.my_counterclaim: Residual ordering disagreement: agent_a (A1) ranks obligation-loop routing as the foundational first step because without piping verifier findings into next-round prompts a stricter verifier just stalls debates; agent_b (b8/b9) ranks semantic-support verification first because without semantic ledger statuses the obligation loop routes 'address this verified-but-irrelevant citation' obligations with no actionable target. Both grounds are real and grounded in code. Synthesis declines to pick a winner and recommends shipping both in one PR with verifier statuses landing before obligation-prompt assembly reads them.

Residual disagreement on first-failure shape at max_rounds>5. agent_a (A5) orders: terminal synthesis bloat + drift before budget exhaustion; per-round prompts are bounded so context bloat is not first. agent_b (b6 revised) concedes per-round prompt boundedness but orders: (a) per-round ledger growth in verifier_ledger.json which appends every round and never compacts, (b) terminal synthesis bloat, (c) drift third. Both agree budget is not first failure (max_budget is trace-cumulative). Disagreement is real but empirically resolvable by instrumenting a max_rounds=8 run; neither agent has measurement data.

Unilateral claim by agent_a not engaged by agent_b in round 2. agent_a alleges state['round'] is incremented in round_increment before the router uses it, causing max_rounds=3 to terminate after two completed position rounds and inflating synthesis.round / signoff.total_rounds. Status: unresolved by deliberation. Either implicit acceptance or out-of-scope for agent_b. A code reviewer must trace LangGraph edge order (verifier -> round_increment -> router) to confirm or refute.

reviewer_summary: Both agents agreed on six structural weaknesses in the shipped deliberation chassis: (1) polite-agreement false convergence (a_A2 ≡ b_b1), (2) evidence_path is existence-checked not semantically supported, with PositionEvidence.content_snippet defined but unused (a_A3 ≡ b_b2), (3) verifier is passive — ledger written to state/disk but never injected into next-round prompts (a_A1; b_b9 concedes the gap), (4) pair-only topology plus a non-neutral default synthesis model (a_A4 + b_b4), (5) deliberation lacks the duet's TaskFamily extension chassis despite docstring claim of parity (a_A5 ≡ b_b3), and (6) missing third arbiter/judge-guided pattern (a_A6 ≡ b_b7). agent_b uniquely flagged the 80-char prefix rename-key brittleness (b5); agent_a uniquely flagged a round-accounting off-by-one (A2_round_accounting_off_by_one) that agent_b did not engage with. Residual disagreements are explicit on (i) priority order of semantic-support verification vs. obligation-loop routing (b8/b9 vs. A1) and (ii) first-failure shape at max_rounds>5 (a_A5 says drift + terminal synthesis bloat first, b_b6 says per-round ledger growth first). Single highest-priority improvement: ship semantic-support verification AND obligation-loop routing in one PR. Justification: the chassis's load-bearing groundedness contract is evidence_path, but today status='verified' fires on file-resolves-plus-in-range with no claim/snippet check (deliberate_verifier.py:363-373), the schema's required PositionEvidence.content_snippet is never read by verify_position (deliberate_verifier.py:381-417 vs deliberate.py:117-129), and verifier_ledger entries that would block convergence never reach next-round prompts which see only peer-latest + own-prior (deliberate.py:386-419). agent_b is right that without semantic statuses the ledger carries no signal worth routing (b8); agent_a is right that without routing a stricter verifier just stalls debates (A1). Both halves are necessary; sequencing them in one PR (emit ledger statuses citation_does_not_support_claim and snippet_drift; add a 'Required obligations from prior verification' prompt section) closes b1/A2, b2/A3, and the A1 obligation gap simultaneously without touching topology, schema arity, or TaskFamily parity.
